scope: Source-grounded scientific acceptance review of three proposed Temporal replacement candidates. Old frozen run artifacts were read only.

method.primary_evidence: Each frozen source_packet.txt, verified identical to its paired source.tex, with exact inclusive line anchors.
method.identity_cross_check: Versioned arXiv records and DOI metadata were cross-checked against the official arXiv API and DOI/Crossref metadata.
method.highest_priority_gate: A Player control must be a numeric quantity actually manipulated or set in the reported study; measured values, fitted quantities, uncertainties, theoretical constants, and sample labels are not controls.

source_identity.title: A digitally controlled silicon quantum processing unit

actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: Pulse duration is set by a code-to-time word, the output pulse width is tunable, and measurements are plotted as a function of the set pulse width. This is an actual numeric intervention, not a measured or fitted surrogate.

line_ranges.evidence: The pulse-waveform caption states that duration is set by a code-to-time word and shows the pulse code-to-time transfer function.
The pulse generator has a tunable 0.4-6 ns width, and pulse-width step size and jitter are measured as functions of set width/across that range.

source_evidence.supports: Representative characterization is for a typical gate-driver output at 4 K routed to room-temperature instrumentation.

The control interval is 0.4-6 ns; normalized jitter is jitter divided by pulse width; the shortest- and long-pulse errors are approximately 7.5e-4 and 4e-4; the acquisition path is 10 ft of high-bandwidth coax into a 256 Gsps oscilloscope.
The measured normalized-jitter fit over 0.4-6 ns is 125 fs/PW + 4e-4.

boundary_findings: The old value 0.125 ns is wrong by a factor of 1000: 125 fs equals 0.000125 ns.
The revised applicability preserves that this is a measured 4 K output-chain characterization, including the stated cable and oscilloscope path; it is not asserted as intrinsic device-only jitter.

minimum_revision: Change jitter_time_constant from 0.125 ns to 0.000125 ns.
Clarify the source-reported measurement path in applicability without changing the response law or domain.

source.citation: Members of the HRL Quantum Team and Collaborators, A digitally controlled silicon quantum processing unit, Nature (2026), DOI:10.1038/s41586-026-10754-7

controls.definition: Set output pulse width of the pulse generator.

readouts.name: normalized_pulse_width_jitter
readouts.definition: Pulse-width jitter expressed as jitter divided by pulse width.

applicability.statement: Model fit to the measured normalized pulse-width jitter from 0.4 to 6 ns.
Representative 4 K gate-driver output characterization routed through 10 ft of high-bandwidth coaxial cabling to a 256 Gsps room-temperature oscilloscope.

source_identity.title: Pattern Formation during Melting of Lamellar Eutectics

actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: Vs is explicitly the imposed directional-solidification velocity. The authors state that both experiments and simulations first solidify the lamellar structure at Vs over 1-10 um s^-1. It is an actual intervention; lambda_JH is the computed readout and d0, D, and P are parameters, not controls.

line_ranges.evidence: Directional solidification is performed at an imposed Vs in a fixed thermal gradient, and the characteristic spacing scales as Vs^-1/2.
Both experiments and simulations first solidify at Vs in the reported 1-10 um s^-1 interval.

source_evidence.supports: Vs is imposed; lambda_JH is the Jackson-Hunt characteristic length and varies as Vs^-1/2.
The system is the CBr4-C2Cl6 eutectic; experiments and quantitative simulations use stated setup assumptions; the table gives D=500 um^2 s^-1 and d0=0.011 um.
The source gives Vs=1-10 um s^-1, lambda_JH=sqrt[d0 D/(Vs P)], and P approximately 0.0293, while stating that realized spacing is close to rather than exactly equal to lambda_JH.

boundary_findings: The readout remains the theoretical Jackson-Hunt characteristic spacing; the card does not relabel it as the realized lamellar spacing.
P is explicitly approximate. The stored composite uses the printed central values deterministically, and its displayed extra digits are computational rather than added measurement precision.

The original d0, D, P, and half parameters occur only through a lower-dimensional product/power combination and cannot be independently identified. Algebraic reparameterization preserves the source law while making the two benchmark parameters locally identifiable.

minimum_revision: Replace the non-identifiable four-parameter encoding by the algebraically identical two-parameter power law.
State explicitly that the composite prefactor is derived from printed central values and that P is approximate.
Keep the imposed Vs interval and the distinction between characteristic and realized spacing unchanged.

source.citation: Rahul Nellissery Rajan, Pattern Formation during Melting of Lamellar Eutectics, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/qtst-bdmt

controls.name: Vs
controls.definition: Imposed directional-solidification velocity used to form the lamellar structure before melting.

readouts.name: lambda_JH
readouts.definition: Jackson-Hunt characteristic spacing to which the resulting lamellar spacing is reported to be close.

applicability.statement: The relation describes the initial directional solidification of the CBr4-C2Cl6 lamellar structure in both experiments and simulations.
The resulting spacing is stated to be close to, rather than exactly equal to, the Jackson-Hunt spacing.

The stored prefactor is the deterministic composite sqrt(d0 D/P) calculated from the printed central values d0=0.011 um, D=500 um^2 s^-1, and P approximately 0.0293; its extra digits are computational and do not imply additional empirical precision.

source_identity.title: Ellipticity-Controlled Bright-Dark Coherence Transition in Monolayer WSe2

actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: Ellipticity is set by the polarized excitation field that prepares the initial state. The paper compares LP, CP, and EP excitation and explicitly continuously tunes ellipticity in its calculations. It is an actual numeric input to the reported study, not the measured coherence readout or a fitted/theoretical parameter.

line_ranges.evidence: The polarized excitation state is parameterized by epsilon; 0 is LP, +/-1 are the two CP helicities, intermediate magnitudes are EP, and C0=sqrt(1-epsilon^2).
The study compares LP, CP, and EP responses and states that arbitrary excitation ellipticity continuously tunes initial coherence, with an ellipticity-dependent response in Fig. 2(c).
The proposed experimental scheme uses a pulsed laser with continuously adjustable polarization ellipticity and polarization-resolved readout.

source_evidence.supports: The l1-norm coherence is defined as the magnitude of off-diagonal density-matrix elements and linked to experimentally accessible linear polarization.
The initial polarized state, ellipticity definition, signed -1 to 1 polarization interval, and exact C0=sqrt(1-epsilon^2) relation are given.
Fig. 2 covers LP, CP, and EP excitations, and the text reports continuous ellipticity tuning and the resulting coherence behavior.

boundary_findings: The full signed interval [-1, 1] is source-supported and should be retained.
The response is symmetric under epsilon to -epsilon and independent of the phase angle because the exact l1-norm expression contains epsilon squared and no phase.

The old compiler failure was representational: treating the inner square exponent as an independently perturbed parameter makes negative epsilon raised to nearby noninteger exponents complex. Encoding epsilon squared structurally as epsilon multiplied by itself removes that artifact without changing the law or restricting the source domain.

minimum_revision: Replace power(epsilon, square_exponent) by multiply(epsilon, epsilon).
Remove square_exponent from the parameter list; retain square_root_exponent=0.5.
Keep the complete source-supported signed interval [-1, 1] and add the continuous-tuning evidence to the control/applicability anchors.

source.citation: Kang Lan, Ellipticity-Controlled Bright-Dark Coherence Transition in Monolayer <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> <mml:mrow> <mml:msub> <mml:mrow> <mml:mi>WSe</mml:mi> </mml:mrow> <mml:mrow> <mml:mn>2</mml:mn> </mml:mrow> </mml:msub> </mml:mrow> </mml:math>, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/lk5d-8qb5

controls.name: excitation_ellipticity
controls.definition: Ellipticity epsilon of the polarized excitation field used to prepare the initial bright-exciton state.

readouts.name: initial_valley_coherence
readouts.definition: Initial l1-norm valley coherence C_0 of the prepared state.

applicability.statement: Applies to the initial polarized bright-exciton state defined by the excitation ellipticity and phase angle.
Ellipticity zero represents linear polarization, the endpoints minus one and one represent the two circular-polarization helicities, and intermediate magnitudes represent elliptical polarization.

The source continuously tunes the excitation ellipticity and evaluates the response for linear, elliptical, and circular excitation; the exact initial l1-norm coherence is sign-symmetric and independent of the phase angle.
